subtitle: When Stone First Spoke the Name of Kamarupa

panels.shot: epic split-scene wide, one half on the Ganga plain with a towering pillar, the other on misty eastern hills and the Brahmaputra
panels.action: Pushyavarman of Kamarupa stands in royal profile over misty hills and forested valleys, while far away the Allahabad victory pillar rises over the Ganga plain, its polished surface catching the sun like a beacon between worlds.

dialogue.text: On a Gupta pillar by the Ganga, a single line names Kamarupa—while far to the east, Pushyavarman turns that first faint mention into a kingdom of his own.

i18n.hi: गंगा किनारे गुप्त स्तंभ पर एक ही पंक्ति में ‘कामरूप’ लिखा गया—और दूर पूरब में पुष्यवर्मन उस हल्की सी चर्चा को अपना राज्य बना रहा था।

panels.shot: low-angle close on the Allahabad pillar base, stretching up into the sky
panels.action: The ancient stone pillar at Allahabad rises from a busy Gupta-era encampment on the Ganga’s bank, polished shaft gleaming as scribes and artisans move like ants around its base.

dialogue.text: Around the year 350, on the Ganga’s middle reaches, a Mauryan pillar found a new voice under the Guptas. On its shining surface, a court poet carved an empire into stone.

i18n.hi: लगभग ३५० ईस्वी में, गंगा के मध्यम प्रवाह पर, एक मौर्य स्तंभ ने गुप्तों के दौर में नई आवाज़ पाई। उसकी चमकती देह पर दरबारी कवि ने पूरे साम्राज्य को पत्थर में उकेर दिया।

panels.shot: tight top-down view on hands and chisel hovering over the inscription lines
panels.action: A court engraver’s steady hands hold chisel and hammer poised over neatly ruled lines on the pillar, while a palm-leaf draft lies nearby with columns of Prakrit in Gupta Brahmi script.

dialogue.text: He listed kings defeated, tribes subdued, forests crossed. Magadha, Kosala, Kanchi—names long known to the plains. Then his stylus hesitated over strange syllables from the far east.

i18n.hi: वह जीते हुए राजा, झुके हुए जन, पार की गई वनों की पंक्तियां गिनता गया। मगध, कोसल, कांची—मैदानों के पुराने नाम। फिर उसकी नोक दूर पूरब से आए अजीब अक्षरों पर अटक गई।

panels.shot: extreme close-up of the inscription line where Kamarupa and Davaka appear
panels.action: The carved line on the pillar is shown in crisp detail, with the words for Kamarupa and Davaka picked out by a shaft of angled sunlight, the rest fading softly around them.

dialogue.text: Among the frontier rulers, beyond direct rule but bound in loose obedience, he carved two new names—Kamarupa and Davaka—frontier polities at India’s eastern edge.

i18n.hi: सीमांत नरेशों में, जो सीधे शासन में नहीं पर ढीली आज्ञा में बंधे थे, उसने दो नए नाम काटे—कामरूप और दावक—भारत के पूर्वी सिरे के सीमा-राज्य।

panels.shot: wide map-like aerial, fading from the pillar over the Ganga to the Brahmaputra valley
panels.action: The scene pulls away from the pillar into a stylised aerial view that sweeps eastward over forests and rivers until it reaches the broad curve of the Brahmaputra and the hills that frame it.

dialogue.text: The pillar knew their names; it did not know their faces. Beyond the Ganga’s memory lay the Brahmaputra valley—marsh and forest, hill and river, where those words were lived, not carved.

i18n.hi: स्तंभ ने नाम पहचाने, चेहरे नहीं। गंगा की स्मृति से परे था ब्रह्मपुत्र घाटी—दलदल और जंगल, पहाड़ और नदी, जहां ये शब्द पत्थर नहीं, जीवन में लिखे जाते थे।

panels.shot: medium shot of Pushyavarman on a bamboo watchtower over the valley
panels.action: Pushyavarman stands on a simple bamboo and timber watchtower above a village by the Brahmaputra, wearing early royal ornaments and a modest diadem, gazing over fields, river channels and distant blue hills.

dialogue.text: Later copperplates from Nidhanpur will name him Pushyavarman, founder of a line. In his own day he was one among many chiefs, raising his gaze above the village to the shape of a kingdom.

i18n.hi: बाद के निधनपुर ताम्रपत्र उसे पुष्यवर्मन कहेंगे, एक वंश का प्रथम राजा। अपने समय में वह बस कई मुखियाओं में एक था, जिसकी नज़र गाँव से उठकर राज्य की रूपरेखा तक गई।

panels.shot: interior medium shot in a bamboo hall, Pushyavarman with elders and priests
panels.action: Inside a thatched hall with carved wooden posts, Pushyavarman sits on a low platform among elders and a Brahmin reciter, palm-leaf texts laid out as they discuss, faces lit by lamplight.

dialogue.text: Around him flowed older stories. Priests spoke of Naraka of Pragjyotisha, of Bhagadatta of epic fame. But those tales lived in chant and song, not in dated records we can test.

i18n.hi: उसके चारों ओर पुरानी कथाएँ बहती थीं। पुरोहित नारक of प्राग्ज्योतिष, महाभारती भगदत्त की गाथा सुनाते थे। पर वे किस्से मंत्र और गीत में थे, न कि जाँचने योग्य दिनांकित लेखों में।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Pushyavarman’s thoughtful face as he listens
panels.action: Pushyavarman’s face is shown in close-up, brows slightly furrowed yet calm as he listens to the recitation, the flicker of the lamp reflected in his eyes.

dialogue.speaker: pushyavarman_and_kamarupa
dialogue.text: Let songs praise the past. I must shape what comes after.

i18n.hi: “पुराने की जय गीतों पर छोड़ो। मुझे आगे का आकार देना है।”

panels.shot: wide shot of a small war-band moving along a forest path
panels.action: Pushyavarman rides at the head of a small war-band along a forest track, spears upright and banners fluttering, while villagers watch from the edges of rice fields and bamboo groves.

dialogue.text: In this landscape of scattered chiefs, strength was counted in men and rice, in elephants and ferries. Pushyavarman stitched together river islands, hill slopes and hamlets into a looser, wider allegiance.

i18n.hi: इस बिखरे सरदारों की धरती पर ताकत गिनी जाती थी लोगों और धान में, हाथियों और नाव-घाटों में। पुष्यवर्मन ने नदी-द्वीप, पहाड़ी ढलान और गाँव जोड़कर ढीले, पर दूर तक फैलते संबंध बुने।

panels.shot: medium shot of Pushyavarman receiving emissaries from the west
panels.action: In an open riverside courtyard, Pushyavarman meets plainly dressed emissaries from the west bearing small gifts, both parties measured and cautious as they exchange respectful bows.

dialogue.text: From the west came word of Samudragupta’s campaigns, of tribute and recognition demanded at the empire’s edges. The Allahabad inscription will call Kamarupa and Davaka their frontier neighbors, not annexed lands.

i18n.hi: पश्चिम से समुद्रगुप्त के अभियानों की खबर आई, सीमा पर चढ़ावे और मान्यता की मांग। इलाहाबाद शिलालेख कामरूप और दावक को सीमान्त पड़ोसी कहेगा, जीती हुई सूबे नहीं।

panels.shot: close shot of Pushyavarman’s hand accepting a symbolic gift
panels.action: Pushyavarman’s hand reaches out to accept a small tray bearing cloth and a crafted token, while his other hand rests firmly on the hilt of his sword, expression composed.

dialogue.text: Somewhere between river and court, gifts and assurances crossed. The pillar will call places like his ‘obedient, yet not directly ruled’—a frontier of negotiation, not conquest.

i18n.hi: कहीं नदी और दरबार के बीच उपहार और भरोसे का आदान–प्रदान हुआ। स्तंभ उनकी जगहों को कहेगा ‘आज्ञाकारी, पर सीधे नशासित’—यह सीमा थी बातचीत की, नहीं विजय की।

panels.shot: wide scenic shot of rituals on a riverbank
panels.action: On a broad riverbank at dusk, Pushyavarman oversees a modest ritual with Brahmins, smoke rising from the altar as boats slip along the Brahmaputra behind them and villagers gather in quiet rows.

dialogue.text: By the Brahmaputra, he grounded his rule in sacrifice and gift, in land grants and ritual, binding priests and peasants to a name that was still taking form—Kamarupa, the land in the eastern curve.

i18n.hi: ब्रह्मपुत्र किनारे उसने यज्ञ और दान में अपना राज स्थिर किया, भूमि-अनुदान और अनुष्ठान में, ब्राह्मण और किसानों को एक ऐसे नाम से बांधते हुए जो अभी आकार ले रहा था—कामरूप, पूरबी मोड़ की धरती।

panels.shot: medium shot focusing on the act of giving a land grant to a Brahmin
panels.action: Pushyavarman hands a folded copper plate and a basket of grain to a standing Brahmin, while a scribe sits nearby with a stylus, ready to scratch the terms onto metal.

dialogue.text: Later, his descendants will issue plates of copper, gifts to Brahmins for maintaining rites. On them they will trace their line back to Pushyavarman, anchoring king and land in written memory.

i18n.hi: बाद में उसके वंशज ताम्रपत्र निकालेंगे, ब्राह्मणों को अनुष्ठान के बदले दान। उन पर वे अपनी जड़ें पुष्यवर्मन तक ले जाएंगे, राजा और भूमि को लिखित स्मृति में बांधते हुए।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide shot transitioning from Pushyavarman’s thatched court to a later, more elaborate one
panels.action: The scene blends from a simple early court of bamboo and thatch to a more elaborate timber and brick hall, suggesting the passage of generations in Kamarupa’s royal house.

dialogue.text: Centuries will pass. Samudragupta’s campaigns will fade, but Kamarupa will endure—its rulers adapting, its frontiers shifting, its memory layered with legend and inscription alike.

i18n.hi: सदियाँ बीतेंगी। समुद्रगुप्त के अभियान धुंधले पड़ेंगे, पर कामरूप बना रहेगा—शासक बदलते हुए, सीमाएँ सरकती हुई, स्मृति में कथा और शिलालेख की परतें जमती हुईं।

panels.shot: interior close-up of a 7th-century scribe engraving the Nidhanpur copperplate
panels.action: A seventh-century scribe kneels, carefully engraving a gleaming copper plate, the letters of the Nidhanpur grant flowing in precise Gupta script under his steady hand.

dialogue.text: In the seventh century, under Bhaskaravarman, a copperplate at Nidhanpur will look back. It will remember Pushyavarman by name and retell his line, set now within crafted genealogies.

i18n.hi: सातवीं सदी में, भास्करवर्मन के समय, निधनपुर का ताम्रपत्र पीछे देखेगा। वह पुष्यवर्मन को नाम से याद करेगा और उसकी वंशावली दोहराएगा, अब सलीके से गढ़ी गई कुल-कथाओं में।

panels.shot: medium shot of Bhaskaravarman receiving the finished plate
panels.action: Bhaskaravarman, a later king in regal attire, receives the freshly inscribed plate from the scribe in a formal court, courtiers and Brahmins arrayed behind him.

dialogue.text: By Bhaskaravarman’s time, the Naraka line of Pragjyotisha will be woven fully into the story, a sacred ancestry claimed to deepen royal roots—even as modern scholars see it as crafted legitimacy.

i18n.hi: भास्करवर्मन के युग तक प्राग्ज्योतिष के नारक वंश को कहानी में पूरा बुन दिया जाएगा, पवित्र पूर्वज-धारा के रूप में जो राजवंश की जड़ें गहरी दिखाए—भले आधुनिक विद्वान उसे रची हुई वैधता मानें।

panels.shot: split close-up: one half on the Allahabad pillar inscription, the other on the Nidhanpur plate text
panels.action: A visual split shows the weathered Allahabad pillar inscription on one side and the sharp lettering of the Nidhanpur copperplate on the other, both texts aligned visually like facing pages.

dialogue.text: Between stone and copper, between Samudragupta’s list and Bhaskaravarman’s grant, a pattern emerges. What begins as a name at the frontier becomes a line of kings and a remembered land.

i18n.hi: पत्थर और तांबे के बीच, समु्द्रगुप्त की सूची और भास्करवर्मन के दान के बीच, एक पैटर्न उभरता है। जो सीमा पर महज़ एक नाम से शुरू हुआ, वही राजाओं की पंक्ति और याद की हुई धरती बन जाता है।

panels.shot: wide contemplative shot of Pushyavarman silhouetted against the Brahmaputra at sunset
panels.action: Pushyavarman stands alone on a riverbank at sunset, his silhouette dark against the glowing expanse of the Brahmaputra and the distant hills, the water calm and reflective.

dialogue.text: Pushyavarman never saw the Allahabad pillar, nor the plates that would honor him. Yet his choices along this river gave weight to a word that a distant court had first carved in passing—Kamarupa.

i18n.hi: पुष्यवर्मन ने न इलाहाबाद स्तंभ देखा, न वे ताम्रपत्र जो उसे मान देंगे। पर इसी नदी किनारे उसके फैसलों ने उस शब्द को वजन दिया जिसे दूर दरबार ने यूँ ही राह में काट दिया था—कामरूप।

panels.shot: final wide shot drifting from the pillar up into the sky, then eastward
panels.action: The view rises from the base of the Allahabad pillar into the sky, then drifts east as if following an invisible line toward the hazy outline of the Brahmaputra valley on the horizon.

dialogue.text: One line of stone on the Ganga, one line of copper by the Brahmaputra—between them, the eastern frontier takes shape, and Kamarupa steps from mist into history’s light.

i18n.hi: गंगा पर पत्थर की एक पंक्ति, ब्रह्मपुत्र पर तांबे की एक पंक्ति—इन दोनों के बीच पूर्वी सीमा आकार लेती है, और कामरूप धुंध से निकल कर इतिहास की रोशनी में कदम रखता है।

title_i18n.en: The Pillar Names the Eastern Kingdom
title_i18n.hi: स्तंभ ने दिया पूर्वी राज्य को नाम

subtitle_i18n.en: When Stone First Spoke the Name of Kamarupa
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब पत्थर ने पहली बार कहा ‘कामरूप’
